transcriptText:
Heads-up. You're on the button. You raise to thirty... and they call. You bet last. So on the flop... who speaks first? You... or them? Make your pick.

Hold'em has four betting rounds. Preflop... flop... turn... and river. Before the flop, heads-up, the button acts first. That's you. You raised, they called. Everyone has acted and the bets match, so the round is closed. Sixty in the pot. Now the flop. Three cards at once. And the big blind acts first.

So the answer is them. The order follows the seats... not who bet last. The turn. One card. Big blind first... button last. The river. One more card... same order again.

With more players, the rule holds. The small blind, the big blind and the cutoff see a flop. The small blind acts first... then the big blind... then the cutoff. The small blind folds. On the turn, the big blind goes first. Start at the button, move left... the first seat still in acts first.

So... four rounds, one order. After the flop, the first seat left of the button acts first, every street. Up next: the showdown.
